Imposition of Liberalism
Why do countries try to impose liberalism on other countries?
1. Self-interest Goals that a country pursues for its benefit: Ajustification is to eliminate or reduce terrorist threats or for economic reasons. Historical examples of this imposition were seen after WWI with the Treaty of Versailles imposing democratic governments (Weimar Republic) as a condition of peace_ "Spreading democracy" has become the core of many American foreign policies ever since. Proponents of imposing liberalism argue that this can have economic and security benefits. (Liberal nations are less likely to threaten each other)
Examples: George W. Bush's "War on Terror" , the Afghanistan invasion by NATO, and the American invasion of Iraq (declared illegal by the UN):
2 Humanitarianism Trying to improve other people's living conditions or trying to stop human rights violations. Ajustification is that it is moral or ethical to help those who can't help themselves. An ideology that advocates promoting human welfare. Humanitarians try to improve the lives of others and reduce suffering by trying to reform societies_ Some non-liberal countries donotobserve human rights and some just choose not to embrace liberalism: This differentiation is critical,
Example: Invasion of Afghanistan to displace the Taliban's unethical treatment of women:
Reactions to the imposing of liberalism The imposition of Iiberalism has been met with a variety of reactions from foreign countries. Democratic elections are often hailed by liberal political leaders as a prerequisite to peace and good governance. However; when they are held in unstable political climates, elections can sometimes exacerbate existing tensions:
